immoreels.title: ImmoReels
immoreels.short: Video-first real estate platform with TikTok-inspired reel format, map search, and light/dark mode.
immoreels.overviewTitle: The future of property search is here
immoreels.description1: ImmoReels revolutionizes how people search for and discover real estate. Instead of static images, the platform takes a video-first approach: properties are presented as short, immersive video reels — inspired by TikTok. Users swipe through listings, experience rooms in motion, and make faster decisions.
immoreels.description2: The platform features a powerful map-based search, smart filters for buying/renting, property type and price, as well as full user profiles with saved properties and inquiries. Both light and dark mode ensure a comfortable experience at any time of day. Real estate agents have a dedicated portal to manage their listings.
immoreels.challenge: Create a property platform that fundamentally differs from existing portals, using video content to enable a more emotional, faster property search — for buyers, renters, and agents alike.
immoreels.solution: Video-first architecture with optimized streaming, responsive carousel design, and a dual theme engine for light and dark mode. Intuitive map search with real-time filtering and a dedicated agent portal.
immoreels.results: Video reels as core format for property presentation | Full light & dark mode | Map-based location search | Agent portal with listing management

pannenhilfe.title: MAT-C Roadside Assistance
pannenhilfe.short: 24/7 roadside assistance platform with member management, admin dashboard, and online contract system.
pannenhilfe.overviewTitle: Roadside assistance that arrives — nationwide and Europe-wide
pannenhilfe.description1: MAT-C is a digital platform for 24/7 roadside assistance across Germany and Europe. The system combines a modern marketing website with a full member portal: users can register, compare and purchase membership packages, manage their contracts, and instantly reach the emergency hotline.
pannenhilfe.description2: For the operator, we built a comprehensive admin dashboard showing users, products, contracts, and revenue at a glance. The system includes contract statistics with flexible time ranges, email templates, digital membership cards, and complete contract management — all in a clean, modern interface.
pannenhilfe.challenge: Build a platform that serves both as a public-facing website for customer acquisition and as an internal management system for members, contracts, and payments — with 24/7 availability.
pannenhilfe.solution: Unified Nuxt application with role-based access control: public website, member area, and admin dashboard in a single codebase. Integrated payment processing and automated contract management.
pannenhilfe.results: 24/7 roadside assistance with <30 min response time | Digital member management | Admin dashboard with real-time statistics | Europe-wide coverage

web.seoTitle: Custom web app development for business
web.seoDescription: Custom web applications for business: customer portals, dashboards and line-of-business tools that run in the browser and talk to the systems you already have.
web.lede: Portals, dashboards and line-of-business tools that run in the browser — connected to the systems you already use.

intro.title: When a web app is the right answer
intro.body1: A web app is not a website. A website informs; a web app does work. It signs people in, knows roles and permissions, processes what they enter and writes results back into your systems. As soon as several people work on the same data and each is allowed to see a different slice of it, you are in web app territory.
intro.body2: The advantage over desktop and mobile: nothing has to be installed. You open a link and everyone works on the same state — colleagues inside the company as well as customers or suppliers outside it. If your application has to run without a network or reach local hardware, a desktop application is the better choice.

uc1.title: Customer and partner portals
uc1.body: Your customers check orders, documents and status themselves instead of calling. That takes noticeable load off your office phones.

uc2.title: Dashboards and reporting
uc2.body: Figures from several systems in one place, current to the day — instead of a spreadsheet someone assembles by hand at month end.

uc3.title: Order and procurement systems
uc3.body: Entry, approvals and handover in one flow, with a traceable status for every case.

uc4.title: Tools built around your process
uc4.body: For when off-the-shelf software covers eighty percent of your process and the remaining twenty are the expensive part.

ap1.title: Connect to what exists
ap1.body: Your ERP, inventory and accounting stay where they are. We integrate through interfaces rather than making you maintain data twice.

ap2.title: Roles from the start
ap2.body: Who may see what, who may change what. We settle this before the first line, because retrofitting it later is expensive.

ap3.title: Operated by you
ap3.body: Hosting in Germany or inside your own infrastructure. The repository and all access stay with you.

q1.q: What does a web app cost?
q1.a: It depends on scope. A contained portal costs considerably less than a line-of-business tool with many roles and interfaces. After the first call you get a quote with a fixed scope and a fixed price, before we start.

q2.q: Can you connect our existing ERP?
q2.a: Usually yes. If the system has an interface, we use it. If not, we look at database or file routes. We tell you what is possible after looking at the system — not once the project is underway.

q3.a: Smaller applications in weeks, larger platforms in months. You see working builds early rather than waiting months for a finished result.

q4.a: Wherever you want: with a German host, in your own server environment, or in your existing cloud. We follow your requirements on data protection and operations.

production.title: Builder, prototype — or software that has to hold
production.body1: Today's app builders and AI generators put something presentable in front of you in an afternoon. That is genuinely useful: if you want to think an idea through internally, those tools are faster than any proposal we could write. We prototype that way ourselves.
production.body2: The difference shows up later. When fifty people work at once, when permissions have to actually hold rather than just hide menu items, when the data model grows after two years without breaking what already exists — the prototype stops carrying. What matters then is unglamorous, and it is exactly our work.

p1.title: Permissions on the server
p1.body: Enforced where they cannot be bypassed, not hidden in the frontend.

p2.title: Migrations without data loss
p2.body: The data model grows. Changes must not damage records already in it.

p3.title: Code you can hand over
p3.body: Readable, tested, documented — including for a team that is not us.

desktop.h1: Desktop software for macOS and Windows
desktop.seoTitle: Custom desktop software development for Windows and macOS
desktop.seoDescription: Custom desktop applications for Windows and macOS: for workstations without reliable network, large data volumes and direct access to devices and the file system.
desktop.lede: Software that runs locally — for workstations without a reliable network, for large files, and for direct access to devices and the file system.

intro.title: Why some software belongs on the machine
intro.body1: Browsers can do a great deal now, but not everything. They may not reach arbitrary folders unprompted, they speak only limited dialects to attached hardware, and when the network drops in a workshop the work stops. For those cases we build software that installs on the machine and keeps running without a connection.
intro.body2: This is not a step backwards. A modern desktop application synchronises as soon as the network returns, updates itself, and shares logic and data model with your web or mobile application when you need more than one surface.

uc1.title: Workstations without a stable network
uc1.body: Workshop, warehouse, building site. The application keeps working and reconciles once the connection is back.

uc2.title: Large files and local processing
uc2.body: CAD data, image stacks, measurement series. Processing on the machine beats any upload.

uc3.title: Devices and interfaces
uc3.body: Scales, scanners, label printers, machine controls. Direct access without going through a browser.

uc4.title: Work with the file system
uc4.body: Watch folder structures, rename files in bulk, file exports away automatically.

ap1.title: One codebase, both systems
ap1.body: Windows and macOS from the same source. That halves not just development but the maintenance that follows.

ap2.title: Installation and updates
ap2.body: Signed installers and automatic updates, so your IT team is not walking round the building for every release.

ap3.title: Offline by design
ap3.body: Local storage with reconciliation, rather than an application that shows an error message the moment the connection drops.

q1.q: Why desktop rather than just a web app?
q1.a: If your application has to run without a network, reach local hardware or process large files, desktop is the honest answer. For anything else we will recommend a web app ourselves — it is cheaper to operate.

q2.q: Does it run on both Windows and macOS?
q2.a: Yes. We develop from a shared codebase for both systems, so features and appearance match and changes only have to be made once.

q3.q: How do updates reach the machines?
q3.a: Through a built-in update function. The application checks for a new version itself and installs it — after approval by your IT team if you prefer.

q4.a: Yes, where your work requires it. Data is held locally and reconciled once a connection returns. How conflicts are resolved is something we decide together.

production.title: The spreadsheet that grew, and where it stops
production.body1: Almost every company has one: the workbook full of macros that has run for years and that exactly one person understands. It was the right answer when it was written — somebody solved a problem instead of waiting for someone else to. That deserves respect, not a lecture.
production.body2: It gets serious when the business depends on it and nobody can intervene: no access control, no history, no backup that understands the file, and a single point of failure attached to one person. That is the point where moving to real software pays for itself.

p1.title: Multi-user operation
p1.body: People working at once, without locked files or "copy (3)".

p2.title: An audit trail
p2.body: Who changed what, and when — provable, years later.

p3.title: No key-person risk
p3.body: Documented code instead of knowledge that walks out with one person.

mobile.h1: Mobile app development for iOS and Android
mobile.seoTitle: Mobile app development for iOS and Android
mobile.seoDescription: Mobile apps for business: field service, warehouse, time tracking and customer apps for iOS and Android. Native or cross-platform, depending on what the job needs.
mobile.lede: iOS and Android. Native when performance decides it — cross-platform when that gets you there sooner.

intro.title: When an app is worth building
intro.body1: An app earns its place when people work standing up. In field service, in the warehouse, on a building site, at a customer. There a phone is the one device already in hand — and camera, location, barcode scanning and offline operation are exactly what the work needs.
intro.body2: Not every idea needs an app. If your users sit at a desk, a web app is almost always cheaper and available sooner. We tell you which way we lean in the first conversation, even when that argues against the bigger project.

uc1.title: Field service
uc1.body: Capture jobs, checklists and reports on site, instead of typing up paper in the evening.

uc2.title: Warehouse and picking
uc2.body: Scan barcodes with the phone camera and post stock immediately, without separate handheld scanners.

uc3.title: Time and activity tracking
uc3.body: Record hours and tasks where they happen — with location where it has to be evidenced.

uc4.title: Customer apps
uc4.body: Orders, status and documents for your customers, when a browser portal is not enough.

ap1.title: Native or cross-platform
ap1.body: We decide on your requirement, not on preference. For most business applications a shared codebase across both platforms is enough.

ap2.title: Offline from the start
ap2.body: Warehouses and building sites have dead spots. The app stores locally and syncs later — otherwise it is useless in the field.

ap3.title: Store release
ap3.body: We handle submission and approval with Apple and Google, or distribute internally through your device management.

q1.q: Native or cross-platform — which is better?
q1.a: For business applications a shared codebase is usually the better call: same features, half the cost, one thing to maintain. Native becomes interesting when you lean heavily on camera, graphics or background processing.

q2.q: Who publishes the app to the App Store?
q2.a: We do — ideally under your own developer account, so the app belongs to you and you stay independent of us.

q3.q: Does the app work without internet?
q3.a: Yes, where your work requires it. Data is held on the device and reconciled at the next connection. We plan for that from the start rather than bolting it on.

q4.q: Do we actually need an app?
q4.a: Often not. If your users mostly work at a computer, we will recommend a web app. We say so in the first conversation, even when it is the smaller project.

production.title: App builders: fine for a test, thin in production
production.body1: An app builder puts something on a phone within days. For an internal test, or to show a board an idea, that is a perfectly sensible route — and cheaper than commissioning us for it.
production.body2: It rarely reaches production. What matters there is the unglamorous part: the app has to keep working in a dead spot and reconcile cleanly afterwards. It has to clear Apple and Google review. It has to still run against a new iOS version in two years, and for that somebody needs the source.

p1.title: Offline and reconciliation
p1.body: Local data and defined rules for when two devices change the same record.

p2.title: Store approval
p2.body: Apple and Google policy is the most common reason an app never ships.

p3.title: Your developer account
p3.body: The app belongs to you, not to a platform that can change its pricing.

ai.seoTitle: AI automation for business – automate manual processes
ai.seoDescription: AI automation for mid-sized companies: read documents, move data between systems, triage incoming requests. With local models where data cannot leave the building.
ai.lede: Work someone does by hand today: reading documents, moving data, triaging requests. With models that never leave your building, where that matters.

intro.title: Automation of a named task, not a project
intro.body1: Most AI initiatives fail not on the technology but because nobody can name which work is supposed to disappear. So we start at the other end: you show us a task a person repeats by hand today, and we work out how many hours are in it.
intro.body2: Only then do we build. Usually that is not a large system but a small, unremarkable automation that sits at one point in your process and saves hours there every day. If it does not pay for itself we tell you — that is what the assessment is for.

uc1.title: Reading documents
uc1.body: Invoices, delivery notes and orders arrive as PDFs or scans and land in your system as structured data instead of being retyped.

uc2.title: Moving data between systems
uc2.body: When the same information is entered by hand in three places today, that is the cheapest automation available.

uc3.title: Triaging requests
uc3.body: Sort incoming email by topic, urgency and ownership, and put a draft reply up for approval.

uc4.title: Producing text and reports
uc4.body: Recurring summaries, minutes and status reports from data you already hold, for a person to check.

ap1.title: Measure the task first
ap1.body: We look at the process and estimate the hours per month inside it. That number decides whether we start at all.

ap2.title: A person keeps the approval
ap2.body: Automation prepares; it does not decide alone. Where correctness matters, your staff stay in the loop with an approval step.

ap3.title: Models in-house when needed
ap3.body: Where your data cannot leave the company, we run models on your own hardware.

q1.q: Does our data leave the company?
q1.a: Only if you want it to. We can run models locally on your own hardware so no content goes to external providers. It takes more setup, but for sensitive documents it is often the only sensible option.

q2.a: Anything frequent, rule-bound and time-consuming today: capturing documents, moving data, sorting, summarising. One-off cases full of exceptions rarely pay off.

q3.q: How do you measure whether it paid off?
q3.a: Before we start we record how long the task takes by hand and how often it occurs. After launch we compare that with actual effort. Without that number, any claim about benefit is guesswork.

q4.q: Do we need large amounts of data?
q4.a: For most applications, no. Modern models already understand language and documents; we add your domain knowledge and rules. Custom training data is only needed in special cases.

production.title: ChatGPT in a browser tab is not automation yet
production.body1: Plenty of staff already help themselves: open the document, copy the content, paste it into an AI tool, copy the answer back. That is resourceful and it does save time. We would not talk anyone out of it while it is one case a week.
production.body2: At two hundred documents a month the arithmetic flips. The copying is the work, not the thinking — and it happens outside your systems, with no record, with company data in somebody else's browser tab. Automation means the task runs without a person in the middle, and the person only approves.

p1.title: Connected, not copied
p1.body: Straight from the mailbox, folder and target system — no trip through the clipboard.

p2.title: Traceable
p2.body: Every case logged: what arrived, what was extracted, who approved it.

p3.title: Data protection settled
p3.body: Local models on request, so no documents go to outside providers.
